claim: MWAA sold 424 acres of surplus 'western lands' at Dulles to Digital Realty Trust for $236.5 million (~$558,000/acre) in 2018.
source_title: 424-Acres at Dulles Airport Could be Sold for Data Centers
supporting_excerpt: Sale price: $236.5 million; approximately $558,000 per acre; Digital Realty Trust LP; 424 acres on the western edge of Dulles.
caveat: Journalistic source reporting a proposed transaction pending board approval in Sept 2018; final closing terms not independently confirmed here.

claim: The 424 acres sold were surplus from an 854-acre parcel acquired starting 2005 for a fourth runway, of which ~414 acres were reserved for the runway itself.
source_title: 424-Acres at Dulles Airport Could be Sold for Data Centers
supporting_excerpt: The 854-acre parcel was originally acquired starting in 2005 for a fourth runway; approximately 414 acres would be used for that purpose, leaving 424 acres unused.
caveat: Establishes the surplus-vs-strategic distinction central to the argument; acreage split as reported by newspaper.

claim: Charlotte Douglas International Airport's fourth parallel runway is a $1.006 billion project; recent runway programs at O'Hare and Atlanta have exceeded $1.1 billion.
source_title: Airport Runway Construction Cost: $12 Million Per Mile in 2026
supporting_excerpt: Runway construction projects at some US airports have exceeded $1.1 billion, notably at Chicago O'Hare and Atlanta; Charlotte Douglas's Fourth Parallel Runway is a $1.006 billion project.
caveat: Secondary trade source; used as a comparable for new-parallel-runway cost, not as an IAD-specific figure. IAD fourth runway isolated cost not publicly broken out.

claim: FAA's estimate of eligible NPIAS airport project costs rose 55% between the 2020 and 2024 reports, from $43.6 billion to $67.5 billion.
source_title: Airport Runway Construction Cost: $12 Million Per Mile in 2026
supporting_excerpt: The FAA's estimated cost of eligible U.S. airport projects increased 55% between the 2020 and 2024 NPIAS reports (from $43.6 billion to $67.5 billion).
caveat: Figure originates in FAA NPIAS reports; cited here via secondary source. Verify against primary NPIAS 2024 before quoting in final.

claim: Entitled data-center land in Loudoun County trades north of $2 million/acre; a November 2025 sale of 97 acres east of Leesburg exceeded $6 million/acre, a county record.
source_title: Loudoun's Data Center Land Values Surge by $19B
supporting_excerpt: Land prices in Ashburn have been trading north of $2M per acre for entitled land; a November 2025 sale of 97 acres east of Leesburg set a value record exceeding $6 million per acre.
caveat: County-wide/parcel-specific transactions, not an appraisal of the subject IAD parcel.

claim: Loudoun County's assessed data-center value surged 78.7% from $23.7B to $42.3B, about 23% of the county tax base in 2025.
source_title: Loudoun's Data Center Land Values Surge by $19B
supporting_excerpt: The assessed value of data centers surged by 78.7%, from $23.7 billion to $42.3 billion, representing almost 23% of the county's tax base in 2025.
caveat: Demonstrates market depth (no urgency premium); not a claim about airport-owned land.

claim: Federally obligated airport land leased/sold for non-aeronautical use must be at fair market value, proceeds reinvested in the airport, and may not interfere with current or future aeronautical use; FAA consent/release required.
source_title: Navigating Airport Land Use Regulations to Grow Non-Aeronautical Revenue
supporting_excerpt: Land sold or leased must be at fair market value and funds used per FAA Revenue Use Policy; a release cannot create incompatible land-uses and cannot interfere with current or future aeronautical activities.
caveat: Trade summary of FAA policy; the underlying primary authority is FAA Order 5190.6B and the Revenue Use Policy. Cite primary for final.

claim: FAA issued a 2023 policy governing land-use changes on federally acquired or federally conveyed airport land.
source_title: Policy Regarding Processing Land Use Changes on Federally Acquired or Federally Conveyed Airport Land
supporting_excerpt: Final FAA policy on processing land use changes on federally acquired or federally conveyed airport land, published Dec 8, 2023.
caveat: Primary source; confirms heightened process bar for converting protected airfield land. Full text not read in detail here.

claim: FAA grant-assurance/revenue-use obligations are enforceable; the Airport Compliance Manual (Order 5190.6B) governs land use and revenue-use compliance.
supporting_excerpt: FAA Order 5190.6B / 5190.6C Airport Compliance Manual governs sponsor obligations including land use and revenue use.
caveat: Primary authority; used to support that grant-assurance violation carries AIP-eligibility/penalty consequences. Specific penalty mechanics not quoted here.

claim: FAA treats thermal exhaust plumes from power generation near airports as a potential navigation hazard, addressed via AC 150/5190-4B and a plume-impact assessment tool, though FAA itself does not regulate plumes.
source_title: Advisory Circular 150/5190-4B, Airport Land Use Compatibility; Technical Guidance Assessment Tool - Thermal Exhaust Plume Impact
supporting_excerpt: Exhaust plumes can create turbulence/reduced-oxygen hazards above the stack; FAA encourages evaluation but does not itself model or regulate plumes.
caveat: Supports plume-cost/liability point; note FAA does NOT enforce plume limits itself, so avoid overstating FAA authority on this.

claim: Dulles plans a future fifth runway (parallel to 12-30, ~10,500 ft), and the fourth runway 1L/19R opened in 2008 (~9,400 ft), indicating airfield-capacity expansion remains a live future use.
source_title: flydulles.com - D2 Projects: Future Fifth Runway / Fourth Runway
supporting_excerpt: The fifth runway will run parallel to existing runway 12-30 along the south side, approximately 10,500 feet long; fourth runway 1L/19R completed 2008, ~9,400 ft.
caveat: Airport-official source confirming future airfield expansion intent; fifth runway not yet scheduled or funded.

claim: Dulles D2 development program and Aerotrain were each cited at approximately $1.4 billion; the fourth runway's isolated cost was not publicly disclosed.
source_title: Washington Dulles International Airport - Airport Technology
supporting_excerpt: More than $1.4bn estimated investment for the D2 project; the train system will cost around $1.4bn; no standalone fourth-runway cost given.
caveat: Documents the data gap on IAD fourth-runway cost; figures are dated (construction-era) and program-level.
